title: The Siege & The Sector Clock
youtubeTitle: Subspace Lattice Academy Ep.4 — Sector Integration (115-Ply Siege)
description: Mission 3 masterclass: dig-in defense, clock arming at ply 100, Contested Space as a stall weapon. Full advanced-manual record.

scenes.headline: When the Clock Decides
scenes.subhead: A 115-ply hybrid-fleet siege. Hubs never fall — coverage does.
scenes.voiceover: Episode four: the siege. One hundred fifteen plies. In the app you join near activation. Here we study the whole dig-in — and how Sector Integration ends eternal turtling.
Full hybrid-fleet rules: Integration Hold, Contested Space, activation at ply one hundred, Initiative Relay. Surgical Strike is still available — it just never lands in this game.

scenes.caption: Siege · plies 1–95
scenes.voiceover: Plies one through ninety-five: both fleets dig in. Escort chains thicken, Beams reposition inside their glow, Hubs stay screened. No walk-in appears — this is the turtling the clock was built to break.
Ply one hundred: Sector Integration can now win. Coverage at or above the marker must hold. Contested Space can break a streak. Surgical Strike is still legal — but the scoreboard is live.

scenes.caption: Clock endgame · coverage as points
scenes.voiceover: After activation, every net cell is a point. Projecting into the enemy net paints Contested Space — stalling their Integration Hold. White converts the coverage race into Sector Integration.
Game over: White wins by Sector Integration. The clock only matters after activation. Until then, hunt the Hub. When both fleets dig in, coverage and Contested Space stop the draw forever.

scenes.headline: Academy complete
scenes.nextEpisode: Practice vs AI · Export a debug log if something feels off
scenes.voiceover: That’s the Fleet Academy series: mindset, Surgical Strike, midgame control, and the sector clock. Open the advanced manual for every annotated ply — then practice against the AI.
